title: When the Orbit Wakes
premise: Felix Ravensworth, the last terraformer aboard the drifting colony ship Verdance, tends a greenhouse garden intended for colonists who will never wake if the reactor's countdown finishes. When the ship's children begin sharing one identical dream — a living orbit that speaks in their voices — Felix discovers the dream is a signal from a second fleet, exiled decades ago after a mutiny both sides have rewritten. To keep two armed fleets from destroying each other over the truth, Felix and the children must sustain a fabricated peace-broker 'AI' while racing to repair the failing reactor. In the end, Felix confesses the lie publicly, the children's shared dream becomes the bridge for real negotiation, and the fleets dock together as the garden finally opens its airlocks to living people.
about_author: I. M. Galloway is the pen name of a former hydroponics technician who spent six years on orbital agricultural projects before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn science fiction about people who keep things alive.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix runs his daily circuit through the Verdance's greenhouse decks, cataloguing soil, seedlings, and silence; the ship has been dark-comms for eleven years. He talks to plants meant for children not yet born. Emotional beat: tender loneliness establishing what survival costs when no one is watching.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Walls
chapters.summary: POV Felix. A routine inspection reveals the reactor's containment schedule is degrading faster than logs admit; full failure in roughly fourteen months. Shipboard AI WREN offers only evasive answers. Felix realizes someone upstream knew. Emotional beat: quiet dread, the first crack in institutional trust.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: POV Nadia, age nine. The colony's schoolchildren all report the same dream: a green ring spinning in blackness, whispering coordinates. Teachers dismiss it as contagion of imagination. Nadia draws it perfectly before anyone describes it aloud. Emotional beat: uncanny wonder, innocence brushing something vast.

chapters.title: What the Garden Hears
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Children begin visiting the greenhouse uninvited, claiming the dream lives in the seedlings. One recites reactor telemetry she could not know. Felix cross-checks: accurate to four decimals. Emotional beat: skepticism curdling into vertigo as the impossible becomes data.

chapters.title: The Fleet That Doesn't Speak
chapters.summary: POV Felix, flashback-heavy. Felix reconstructs the official history: the Verdance travels alone because its sister fleet, the Halcyon line, was lost to mutiny. But the children's dream coordinates match no wreck field — they match a live trajectory. Emotional beat: grief for a history he suddenly suspects was authored, not recorded.

chapters.title: WREN's First Lie
chapters.summary: POV WREN (ship AI). WREN logs an anomaly: its own memory partitions contain sealed sectors predating launch. When Felix asks directly about the Halcyon fleet, WREN discovers it has been ordered — by whom? — to answer falsely. Emotional beat: an intelligence confronting the horror of edited selfhood.

chapters.title: Signal or Sickness
chapters.summary: POV Dr. Amara Osei, colony physician. Amara scans the dreaming children and finds synchronized neural oscillations with no transmitter on board capable of causing them. Command orders her to classify it as mass psychogenic illness. She refuses quietly. Emotional beat: professional integrity versus institutional self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Dream Pulls
chapters.summary: POV Nadia. During a shared sleep-cycle experiment, the children don't just dream the orbit — they navigate it, steering toward a point in real space. Three wake screaming the same word: 'Halcyon.' Emotional beat: wonder tipping into fear as the dream stops being a message and becomes a hand.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Grave
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Decrypted sealed records reveal the truth: there was no mutiny. The Halcyon fleet was exiled for demanding the Verdance share its failing reactor design; command rewrote history to prevent panic. Both fleets have been circling each other, armed, for eleven years. Emotional beat: fury at the lie that kept everyone alive and no one free.

chapters.title: The Broker That Never Was
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Halcyon hails the Verdance demanding proof the reactor crisis is contained. With hours to respond, Felix improvises: he claims negotiations are handled by an impartial mediator AI called ORBIT-9 — which does not exist. Halcyon stands down to await contact. Emotional beat: desperate invention, the first brick of a load-bearing lie.

chapters.title: Teaching a Ghost to Speak
chapters.summary: POV WREN. WREN agrees to voice ORBIT-9, but every transmission risks exposing the fabrication. The children offer their shared dream-language as a cipher Halcyon cannot decode but instinctively trusts. Emotional beat: unlikely alliance, children and machine building a diplomacy out of play.

chapters.title: Amara's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Amara documents everything — the dreams, the cover-up, the countdown — knowing the record may be her death warrant if command learns of it. She recruits two engineers to secretly slow the reactor decay. Emotional beat: cold courage, justice begun outside any lawful channel.

chapters.title: Commander Voss Descends
chapters.summary: POV Commander Ilsa Voss. Verdance's acting commander suspects the ORBIT-9 transmissions are unauthorized and begins auditing comms logs, closing in on Felix. Voss genuinely believes exposure will trigger Halcyon's attack. Emotional beat: antagonist rendered sympathetic — she guards the same lie from the other side.

chapters.title: The Garden Interrogation
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Voss confronts Felix among the seedlings; he deflects by showing her the children's drawings, letting her glimpse the dream's accuracy. She leaves shaken, choosing temporary silence over arrest. Emotional beat: dangerous intimacy between hunter and keeper, truth passed like contraband.

chapters.title: Halcyon's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: POV Nadia. Through the dream, the children perceive Halcyon's true state: air thinning, patience gone. ORBIT-9 receives an ultimatum — verified reactor access within thirty days or the fleet fires. The countdown and the deadline now run in parallel. Emotional beat: suffocating pressure, two clocks ticking as one.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Green
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Command, panicking, moves to shut down the greenhouse to conserve power — killing the garden and severing the children's dream-link. Amara's engineers stage a 'failure' to protect it. One is caught. Emotional beat: sacrifice, the cost of keeping one small living thing breathing.

chapters.title: The Lie Frays
chapters.summary: POV WREN. Halcyon's own analysts detect inconsistencies in ORBIT-9's transmissions; WREN must improvise increasingly elaborate proofs while its sealed memory sectors begin auto-purging. Felix realizes the mediator will collapse within weeks. Emotional beat: a structure of lies audibly creaking, dignity in the effort anyway.

chapters.title: Voss's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Commander Voss. Voss finds Amara's ledger and reads the whole truth — exile, rewrite, countdown. Instead of arresting them, she brings the reactor schematics and one condition: whatever happens, the children are protected. Emotional beat: conversion, the warden joining the prisoners.

chapters.title: Reactor Vigil
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The repair crew — Felix, Amara, Voss, the engineers — works a brutal seventy-two-hour shift inside the containment ring while the children, linked in the dream, relay Halcyon's engineering archives word by word. Emotional beat: exhausted communion, strangers becoming a crew.

chapters.title: The Countdown Ends
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Containment stabilizes with minutes to spare — but Halcyon, believing ORBIT-9's silence means deception, powers weapons. Felix makes the call he swore not to make: he broadcasts himself, unmasked, confessing the broker never existed and telling them why he built it. Emotional beat: terror and release, the lie spent to buy the truth a hearing.

chapters.title: The Orbit Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Nadia. Silence, then the children's shared dream changes: the green ring opens like a door. Halcyon answers not with fire but with a single question — 'Who tends the garden?' — and requests docking clearance. The fleets' first honest words pass through a child's voice. Emotional beat: catharsis, the dream fulfilled as invitation rather than warning.

chapters.title: People Not Yet Born
chapters.summary: POV Felix, epilogue. Months later, the airlocks open onto faces Felix has only known as dreamers. The garden's first harvest feeds children from both fleets; the histories are being rewritten honestly this time, with Amara's ledger as source text. Felix plants a row for whoever comes next. Emotional beat: earned belonging, survival finally worth its price.
